doc.title: Rick Montalbano interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 12, 2011

chapter: Staying in Rome and best and worst gigs
title: Most memorable recent gigs: with his son and Pastabilities
summary: He cannot pick one gig. He names playing with his son and Jane Monheit and his weekly Wednesday gig in Syracuse, and quotes Monterose on staying interested.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Well here’s a hard one to sort of wrap up here. Do you remember, is there any gig or a series of gigs stand out as one of the most memorable or greatest things ever?

Hmm. That’s a tough question. I don’t know, Monk. I don’t think I could pick a particular gig. I could tell you some of the things I’ve really gotten a lot of enjoyment out of lately, when I get to the chance to play with my son and my daughter-in-law [Jane Monheit], in that setting, when their piano player — a couple of weeks ago he was in Spain I guess doing something and they had a gig in Massachusetts so I went in and filled in and it was just a ball to play in that setting with them, and to play with my son, and to play music like that, those great tunes and beautiful arrangements and a great piano, where people listen to you. You know so that’s been a particular joy. The other one is my regular Wednesday night gig in Syracuse with Pastabilities, with John Rhode and Jimmy Johns. You know we’ve been there, I don’t know, eight or nine years maybe, every Wednesday night in that setting, saxophone, vibes and piano, and when Ricky’s in town he plays with us. That’s been a particular joy lately. I don’t know what I would do © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -21-

without that gig. You know it’s one of those opportunities to do original material and arrangements, organized. You know we’ve played together so long. And it’s a little odd combination of things so the way we voice things and work out arrangements is a source of interest. J.R. Monterose used to say “you’ve got to stay interested.” When he first started saying it — but the older I get I realize that’s so true. That’s so true. I look for things that interest me. Musical opportunities.
Yeah. It’s really nice to have a gig like that every week because during the week I’ll bet you’re thinking about, when you’re driving, you say “well we could try this.”
All week long that’s like the X in my week.
Wednesday night, seven o’clock. And everything is kind of what are we going to do, this tune and then afterwards it’s like I could have done this or that. So it’s a source of great pleasure.
